opportunity: varnode_flags::indirectonly has two readers in the merged tree -- HighVariable::has_name (variable.rs) and Merge::merge_test_adjacent (merge.rs) -- and NO writer: Funcdata::markIndirectOnly / checkIndirectUse (funcdata_varnode.cc:801-858) were never ported and ActionMarkIndirectOnly shipped as a documented no-op although universal_sched already scheduled it one slot ahead of ActionMergeAdjacent. So is_indirect_only() answered false everywhere and both readers took the strictly-more-conservative branch: kuna refused every speculative merge with an illegal input, including the ones upstream allows.
root_cause: Both refusals are about an ILLEGAL INPUT -- an input Varnode ActionDirectWrite never reached, i.e. the leftover entry value of a frame slot the function overwrites before it reads. Refusing the merge is the right default (an uninitialized value must not be printed as a real one); upstream's exception is that when EVERY reader in the def-set is a plain CPUI_INDIRECT the leftover value is not read at all, so there is nothing to print wrongly. That exception needed the flag nothing wrote.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-indirectonly.xml (two functions x two passes: `take` changes off->on, the directly-read counterexample `keep` must not) + 8 unit tests in kuna_indirectonly/tests.rs

census.method: throwaway KUNA_IO_DEBUG instrumentation in mark_indirect_only, release build, kuna decompile-all over the decbench stripped coreutils binaries (docs/features/indirectonly/census.txt); reverted before the shipped commit
census.finding: no flagged input is also `unaffected`, so HighVariable::has_name's indirectonly branch never fires on x86-64 ELF and removes no declaration; the live consumer is Merge::merge_test_adjacent

corpus_sweep.structural_control: for all 10 changed functions the sequence of control keywords with their nesting depth and the ordered sequence of callees are identical in both arms (skeleton-check.txt), so no statement moved across a branch or a call

hunks.class: wrong output fixed: both halves of a 16-byte struct on the frame are now written before its address is passed to hash_delete

a vN = slot; / slot = vN; round-trip disappears (5 statements)
